newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends lower on BOJ governor comments.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends lower on BOJ governor comments.

text.p: Key December three-month Euroyen interest rate futures fell towards the Tokyo close on Wednesday due to bullish comments on Japan's economy by Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita.

"The BOJ governor's comments hit the market. It was basically vulnerable because the topside was firmly capped despite firmness in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures," said a long-term credit bank dealer.
The December lost 0.05 to 99.03 after moving between 99.02 and 99.09.

"Overall prices are stable except for the impact from the sales tax increase, but potential concern about prices of goods may arise if confidence in the prospects for the economy increases," Matsushita was quoted as saying in a meeting between BOJ officials and officials of the Japan Federation of Economic Organisations (Keidanren). The remarks were quoted by a Keidanren official who briefed reporters on the meeting.
"His remarks on prices are behind the December's fall by four to five ticks," a city bank dealer said.
The remarks came before TIFFE's day session finished at 3.30 p.m. (0630 GMT).

Traders said other factors dampening the December contract were vague market rumours that the BOJ may reduce the amount of its outright bond purchases and the Ministry of Finance's Trust Fund Bureau may do that as well or halt purchases outright.
A MOF official said: "It is not true that we have decided something new." BOJ officials were not immediately available to comment on the rumour.
Turnover was 68,783 contracts. Of that, only 10,137 changed hands in the morning.
In the interbank market, the key overnight call rate fell to 0.49 percent from Tuesday's 0.53 percent.

The rate's fall was attributed to the BOJ's extra accommodative credit stance, which it has maintained since last Friday. The bank left a surplus of around 210 billion yen by draining 400 billion yen at its Wednesday market operation.

But long-term money rates were underpinned by concerns over a possible rise in interest rates in and after July. Traders said one city bank issued some 200 billion yen worth of three-month certificates of deposit (CDs) at 0.57 percent, up from Tuesday's 0.56 percent. -- Risa Maeda Tokyo Treasury Desk
